verses.text: After this I saw another angel coming down from heaven. He had great authority, and the earth was lit up by his glory.
He shouted with a mighty voice: "Fallen! Fallen is Babylon the great! She has become a home for demons, a prison for every evil spirit, a prison for every unclean and hated bird.

For all the nations have drunk the wine of her sexual sin, which brings God's anger. The kings of the earth did sexual sin with her, and the traders of the earth grew rich from her great wealth and her love of luxury."
Then I heard another voice from heaven say: "Come out of her, my people, so that you do not take part in her sins, and so that you do not receive any of her disasters.
For her sins are piled up as high as heaven, and God has remembered the wrong things she has done.
Pay her back as she has paid others. Pay her back twice as much for what she has done. Mix her a drink twice as strong in the cup she mixed for others.
Give her as much pain and sorrow as the glory and luxury she gave herself. In her heart she says, 'I sit as a queen. I am not a widow, and I will never be sad.'
So her disasters will come in one day: death, sorrow, and hunger. She will be burned up with fire, because the Lord God who judges her is mighty.
The kings of the earth who did sexual sin with her and shared her luxury will cry and weep over her when they see the smoke of her burning.
They will stand far away, afraid of her pain, and say: 'How terrible, how terrible for you, great city, Babylon, city of power! In one hour your punishment has come!'
The traders of the earth will cry and be sad over her, because no one buys their goods any more:
goods of gold, silver, jewels, and pearls; fine linen, purple, silk, and bright red cloth; all kinds of sweet-smelling wood; all kinds of things made of ivory, costly wood, bronze, iron, and marble;
cinnamon, spice, incense, perfume, and frankincense; wine, olive oil, fine flour, and wheat; cattle, sheep, horses, and carriages; and human beings sold as slaves.
They will say, 'All the good things your heart wanted are gone from you. All your riches and beauty have disappeared, and you will never find them again.'
The traders who sold these things and became rich from her will stand far away, afraid of her pain. They will cry and be sad,
and say: 'How terrible, how terrible for the great city! She was dressed in fine linen, purple, and bright red, and covered with gold, jewels, and pearls!
In one hour all this great wealth has been destroyed!' Every ship's captain, everyone who travels by ship, the sailors, and all who earn their living from the sea, stood far away.
When they saw the smoke of her burning, they cried out, 'Was there ever a city like this great city?'

They threw dust on their heads and cried out, weeping and sad: 'How terrible, how terrible for the great city! All who had ships on the sea became rich through her wealth. And in one hour she has been destroyed!'
"Be glad about her, heaven! Be glad, God's holy people, apostles, and prophets! For God has judged her for the way she treated you."

Then a mighty angel picked up a stone the size of a large millstone and threw it into the sea. He said: "This is how the great city of Babylon will be thrown down with violence, and it will never be found again.

The music of harp players, singers, flute players, and trumpeters will never be heard in you again. No worker of any trade will ever be found in you again. The sound of a millstone will never be heard in you again.

The light of a lamp will never shine in you again. The voices of the bridegroom and the bride will never be heard in you again. Your traders were the great people of the world, and by your witchcraft all the nations were fooled.
In her was found the blood of prophets and of God's holy people, and of all who have been killed on the earth."
